title: Book One · Chapter 11: Leo's Idea
story:
Leo brings a picture to school. It shows a red kite above a field.

"We can make that," he tells Ronan.

Ronan looks at the kite. It has a long tail with three little bows.

"Can you?"

"My cousin has one."

"Did you make it?"

"No. But I held it."

Ronan puts the picture on the desk. A kite can move. It can go high in the sky. Ronan wants everyone to look up at their kite.

"I have brown paper," he says.

"I have string."

"Then what do we do?"

Leo draws a kite on the back of the picture. His lines run off the edge.

"You cut. I fly."

Ronan looks at him.

"Why do you fly?"

"I can hold it."

"I can hold it too."

Leo lifts the stone from the desk. "This is easy to hold. It doesn't go anywhere."

Ronan takes the picture away. He wants to fly the kite, too. He puts the scissors down. Ronan can hold string too.

Miss Wu walks past. "Did you choose something?"

"A kite," Leo says.

"Perhaps," Ronan says.

Miss Wu pulls a chair close. She is holding six home notes. One has soup on it.

"What is wrong?"

Both boys speak at once. She waits. Then Ronan explains. Leo points to the paper. It belongs to Ronan. The string belongs to Leo. "We both bring something," Leo says. "That is fair."

"You need paper and string," Miss Wu says. "What work comes next?"

They don't know all of it. Miss Wu gets a clean piece of paper. "Draw your paper and sticks here," she says. "Do you need more things? Draw those too."

Ronan draws paper and scissors. Leo draws two long sticks.

"Where will those come from?" she asks.

"My dad may have some," Ronan says.

"Did you ask him?"

"No. I need to ask him."

She writes a small question mark beside the sticks. There is another beside glue. The page soon has more questions than things.

"This isn't much of a plan," Leo says.

"Now we have a list," Ronan says. "Before, we only had a picture."

Miss Wu smiles, but she has to go. Two children are calling her from the cupboard.

The boys look at the page. Leo draws two hands holding one string.

"Take turns," he says.

"And we take turns making it too."

Leo nods. They write both their names under the kite. Ronan's name goes across one stick. Leo writes his name below Ronan's.

At home, Dad looks at the page.

"I have two thin strips of bamboo. They're left from a job. You can use them after I make the ends smooth."

"Can you make the kite?"

"I can help with those strips. But I made my last kite many years ago."

Ronan is surprised by that answer. Dad can make many things with wood. Ronan often watches him work.

Ronan carries the picture outside. Mrs Lan is bringing in a shirt from the line. The wind fills its sleeves.

"That's a good flyer," she says, looking at the shirt.

"It doesn't have a tail."

"It has two. They're called sleeves."

Ronan laughs and holds the picture up against the evening sky. He lifts the picture above his head. He wants their kite up there, too. He lowers the picture and takes it inside. Tomorrow they can start.
studyGuide:
## 先看情节提示也可以

Leo提议两人做风筝；Ronan要求制作和试飞都要轮流，而不只负责剪纸。

## 从认词到读句子

1. **Leo / brings a picture / to school.** Leo／带一张图片／到学校。
2. **Ronan / takes / the picture away.** Ronan／把图片拿开；take…away整体表示拿开。

---

重点表达：kite＝风筝；string＝线；Take turns＝轮流；bamboo＝竹子。

辅助理解：strips of bamboo＝细竹条；smooth＝光滑的；sleeve＝袖子。

理解问题：

1. 两人最初对分工有什么不同想法？
2. 他们最后向老师交了什么计划？
